content:
For any sorted set \(x_1<\cdots<x_{20}\), a triplet with largest element \(x_k\) uses two smaller elements summing to \(x_k\). Among the \(k-1\) smaller elements, each can appear in at most one such pair, so there are at most \(\lfloor (k-1)/2\rfloor\) triplets ending at \(x_k\).

Thus the total number of additive triplets is at most
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{20}\left\lfloor \frac{k-1}{2}\right\rfloor
=0+0+1+1+\cdots+9+9=90.
\]

The set \(\{1,2,\dots,20\}\) achieves this: for each \(c=k\le 20\), the pairs \((a,b)\) with \(a<b\) and \(a+b=k\) are exactly \(\lfloor (k-1)/2\rfloor\), giving
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{19^2}{4}\right\rfloor=90.
\]

Therefore the maximum is \(\boxed{90}\).
